newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower as harvest rolls on.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower as harvest rolls on.

text.p: Nearby KCBT hard red winter wheat futures crept lower throughout the session and ended just above session lows as harvesting picked up speed in the central U.S. Plains, traders said.
Warm, dry weather should allow harvesting to progress rapidly over the next four days in Kansas and Oklahoma, and traders said reports of yields on some fields were coming in well above average.
"I heard 59 to 66 bushels per acre in some parts of Sumner County (Kansas) -- that's way above the average," a KCBT trader said just before the close.
Traders said losses were compounded by the lack of export business.
KCBT wheat settled 4-1/4 cents lower to 5-1/2 cents higher, with nearby July down 4-1/4 cents at $3.56 per bushel.
Volume was light to moderate at midsession but increased late in the session.
Traders said they saw more buying of the July/Sept and Sept/Dec bull-spreads Thursday as speculative players rolled their short positions from nearby July to a deferred contract.
Featured players included Linnco Futures, which sold two million July bushels. E. D. & F. Man International sold one million Sept and 1.7 million Dec bushels.
